hooks.text: Engineers designed a spaceship propelled by one nuclear bomb every second.
A 1958 rocket design delivered an estimated 2,000 seconds of specific impulse.
A crewed spaceship was engineered to ride directly on nuclear explosions.

title: The Cold War Rocket Powered by Atomic Bombs
description: In 1958, Project Orion engineered a crewed interplanetary spacecraft driven by a rapid-fire sequence of atomic bomb detonations.

beats.text: Engineers designed a spaceship propelled by one nuclear bomb every second.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Project Orion interplanetary spacecraft, 1958

beats.text: In 1958, physicists Ted Taylor and Freeman Dyson led Project Orion at General Atomics.
beats.visual: photograph of physicist Freeman Dyson at the Institute for Advanced Study, 1960s

beats.text: Their analyzed design delivered an estimated specific impulse of approximately 2,000 seconds.
beats.visual: diagram of the Project Orion spacecraft architecture and propulsion system, 1959

beats.text: Shaped nuclear charges blasted hot plasma directly against a heavy steel pusher plate.
beats.visual: technical diagram of the Project Orion nuclear pulse pusher plate mechanism, 1959

beats.text: Giant shock absorbers reduced extreme blast accelerations to just a few g's for the crew compartment.
beats.visual: photograph of the Project Orion Hot Rod flight test vehicle, 1959
queries: Project Orion Putt Putt model test

beats.text: To keep atomic fireballs from vaporizing the plate, researchers discovered an unexpected fix.
beats.visual: photograph of the atmospheric nuclear test mushroom cloud from Operation Ivy Mike, 1952
queries: Ivy Mike atmospheric nuclear test mushroom cloud

beats.text: Spraying a thin film of oil between detonations prevented surface ablation entirely.
beats.visual: photograph of the Project Orion wooden display model at the National Air and Space Museum

beats.text: The 1963 Test Ban Treaty canceled the program in 1964, ending the dream before a single launch.
beats.visual: photograph of officials signing the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty in Moscow, 1963

Dean Rusk signing Test Ban Treaty Moscow
